statement: Frontline staff need to trade shifts with a qualified coworker without a manager phoning around so that shifts stay covered when plans change
problem: Swapping a shift means calling the manager, who then calls around
outcome: Covered shifts with no manager time spent
scenarios: A cashier's kid gets sick on Thursday night and she spends an hour texting coworkers to cover Friday
A warehouse picker trades a weekend for a weekday by writing it on the break-room whiteboard and the manager never sees it
Two nurses agree to switch nights but the schedule still shows the old names, so the wrong one is paged

statement: Shift managers need to offer an uncovered shift to every eligible worker at once so that last-minute gaps are filled before the shift starts
problem: A call-out an hour before opening leaves a gap nobody hears about in time
outcome: Gaps filled before the shift starts
scenarios: A guard calls out at 5am and the supervisor rings eight people before anyone answers
The hotel front desk is short on a holiday and the manager posts in three group chats
A store manager learns at opening that two people are out and works the register herself

statement: Payroll admins need approved hours in the format their outside accountant imports so that payroll closes without retyping timesheets
problem: Hours are retyped from screenshots into the accountant's spreadsheet
outcome: Payroll closes on time with no retyping
scenarios: Every second Friday the office manager copies 40 timesheets into a spreadsheet by hand
The outside bookkeeper rejects a file because the columns are in the wrong order
A typo while retyping hours means a cook is underpaid and has to be corrected next cycle

statement: HR managers need a tamper-evident record of hours and edits per worker so that union and labour audits can be answered from the system
problem: Auditors ask who changed a timesheet and when, and nobody can say
outcome: Audits answered in a day from one record
scenarios: The union rep asks for every edit made to a member's hours in March and HR has only the final numbers
A labour inspector wants twelve months of hours for one site and IT has to stitch exports together
A supervisor quietly changes a clock-out time and the worker disputes it months later

statement: Shift managers need to know before a worker crosses into overtime so that they can rebalance hours instead of paying unplanned overtime
problem: Overtime shows up only on the payroll report, after it is paid
scenarios: A distribution centre finds out at month end that one forklift driver logged 22 hours of overtime
A manager approves an extra shift without noticing it pushes the person over 40 hours
Finance asks why labour cost jumped and nobody saw it coming

statement: Site managers need clock-ins to be tied to the work site so that hours reflect where people actually worked
problem: Anyone can clock in from anywhere
outcome: Hours that match real presence on site
scenarios: A guard clocks in from the bus on the way to the post
A cleaner is paid for a site she never reached because the app accepted her clock-in from home
A manager cannot tell which of two warehouses a picker worked at on Tuesday

statement: Compliance leads need evidence of where and when each clock-in happened so that client contracts that bill by site presence can be verified
problem: Clients dispute invoices because presence cannot be shown
scenarios: A client refuses to pay for night patrols because the guard company cannot show the guard was on site
A hospital contract requires proof that agency nurses arrived before handover
An auditor samples twenty shifts and asks for the location of each clock-in

statement: Frontline staff working without reception need to clock in and have it record later so that they are paid from when they started
problem: Basement and rural sites have no signal, so clock-ins fail
outcome: Correct start times with no manual fixes
scenarios: A stocker in a basement storeroom walks back upstairs to find signal before she can start
A rural care worker's clock-in fails and her manager edits the time by hand every day
A loading dock has one bar of signal and the app spins until the shift has started

statement: Frontline staff need schedule changes made over the weekend to reach their phones right away so that nobody misses a shift that moved
problem: Weekend edits only appear after the next login sync
outcome: No missed shifts after weekend changes
scenarios: A barista's Sunday shift moves to 6am on Saturday night and she arrives at 9
The schedule on a guard's phone still shows last week's rota on Sunday
A server shows up to a closed restaurant because the Sunday change never reached her

statement: Part-time staff need to state when they can and cannot work so that managers stop scheduling them during classes or second jobs
scenarios: A student is put on Tuesday mornings every week despite telling the manager about her lecture
A cook with a second job keeps getting double-booked on Fridays
A new hire's availability lives on a sticky note on the manager's monitor
